subject: Next Steps: DataPulse POC — Prompt & Log Transfer, Eval Success Criteria
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice@datapulse.io>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@datapulse.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: DataPulse discovery recap + POC ask

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have a common checklist for the POC kickoff: 

1) POC objective: validate that Redwood reduces per-response latency below 300ms p95 and reduces per-token inference cost by ~30% vs your current managed endpoints, while keeping answer accuracy within 3% of your current baseline on the representative prompt set.

2) Success criteria (initial):
- Latency: p95 < 300ms for 512-token windows on dedicated medium profile
- Cost: token-cost delta <= -30% measured over a 2k prompt sample
- Quality: BLEU/ROUGE/semantic similarity delta within ±3% of baseline (we'll define exact metrics after you drop sample logs)

3) Data we need from you to build the eval:
- Representative prompt set (2,000 prompts ideally; can be logs or hand-curated). CSV/JSONL with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output (if available), task_type (summarize/qa/compose), sensitivity_flag.
- 200 warmup prompts marked for latency traces.
- A short privacy matrix highlighting PII/sensitivity guidance for any prompt logging (attachment: privacy matrix template).

4) Timeline (proposed):
- Nov 9: DataPulse delivers sample batch (200 prompts) + privacy matrix
- Nov 10–13: Redwood ingests sample, returns schema feedback and S3 transfer instructions
- Nov 16: Full 2k batch delivered; Redwood runs eval and returns initial report by Nov 23

5) Owners:
- Data transfer/permissions: Alice / Tom (DataPulse)
- Eval metrics and tooling: Ben Carter (Redwood)
- Onboarding / success ops: Marissa Cole (Redwood)
- Commercial / contract: Me (Evelyn)

Can you confirm owners and the Nov 9 sample delivery? If that date is tight, we can push a week. Also flagged one security question you raised on the call re: retaining raw prompts — see the attached privacy matrix template so we can handle redaction/retention controls.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart | Strategic Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Wong <alice@datapulse.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@datapulse.io>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DataPulse discovery recap + POC ask

Evelyn —

Appreciate the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side and setting expectations: 

- Owners: I'm the technical lead for the POC (prompt/log ownership), Tom will own security/compliance and the privacy matrix.
- We can deliver the 200-sample batch by Mon Nov 9, but it will include personally-identifying tokens in ~8% of prompts; we need guidance on whether Redwood will store raw prompts or only hashed/stripped variants for evaluation.

Attachments: I attached a sanitized sample CSV (datapulse_prompt_sample_1.csv) and our initial privacy matrix (datapulse_privacy_matrix.pdf). The CSV includes prompt_id, prompt_text, and an internal expected_output field for ~40% of rows. Please confirm receipt and any schema changes you need.

Also: we use an internal label for task_type (e.g., "summ-brev", "extract-kw"). If Redwood can map these to your generic task taxonomy, that's ideal.

Thanks — will await the S3 transfer instructions and any redaction guidance.

—Alice
Alice Wong | Senior ML Engineer
DataPulse Solutions

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice@datapulse.io>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DataPulse discovery recap + POC ask

Thanks Alice — I got the sample and privacy matrix, very helpful. Quick notes after a first pass: 

- Schema: your CSV looks good. I'll produce a minimal ingestion validation script and share in the S3 instructions. The fields we need lined up: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output (optional), task_type, sensitivity_flag. If sensitivity_flag is not present for some rows, we'll treat as "unknown" and suggest redaction for high-risk prompts.

- Storage: Redwood can accept either: (A) raw prompts if you grant short-term S3 access and sign our temporary retention addendum (retention 30 days), or (B) a redacted/hash-only variant. For evaluation fidelity we prefer (A) under the retention addendum; Tom, please advise which you prefer.

- Task mapping: Marissa and I will map your internal labels to Redwood taxonomy. If you can provide a 1-page mapping table it's faster.

Action items assigned here: 
- Ben: prepare ingestion script + S3 instructions by Nov 6
- Marissa: draft metric definitions template and eval dashboard mockup by Nov 13
- Alice: provide 200-sample CSV + privacy matrix by Nov 9 (confirmed)

I'll attach the ingestion checklist in my next note.

Cheers,
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@datapulse.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Wong <alice@datapulse.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DataPulse discovery recap + POC ask

Ben / Evelyn —

We prefer option (A) — raw prompts for fidelity — provided Redwood signs the temporary retention addendum. I'll have legal review today but expect no blockers. Two notes: 

1) We'll only grant an S3 role scoped to the single bucket/prefix for 30 days.
2) We need to ensure your eval tooling strips and redacts any output logs before they leave Redwood systems; can you confirm that redaction is part of the retention addendum?

If you can send the addendum + S3 instructions by EOD Nov 6, we can proceed with Nov 9 transfer.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Harris | Head of Data Engineering
DataPulse Solutions

Subject: Re: DataPulse discovery recap + POC ask

Tom / Alice —

We're aligned on the retention flow. Ben and I attached the retention addendum and the S3 transfer playbook to the internal HubSpot deal (link below). Key points: 

- Redwood will store raw prompts for up to 30 days and will redact any PII from eval output before persisting reports. Raw prompt access for engineers is logged and limited to the eval team.
- Ingestion script will validate schema, flag unknown sensitivity, and optionally run a token-level PII scanner you can configure.

Link: https://redwood.app/hubspot/DEAL-DP-2026-041 (internal)

Ben / I will be on the call Nov 9 to accept the transfer. If legal needs language tweaks, please send edits to legal@datapulse.io and cc me.

Regards,
Marissa Cole | Onboarding & Success
Redwood Inference
